finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches a URL taken directly from the query string. It has no allowlist, scheme check or IP check, and requests follows redirects by default. An attacker can make the server request internal hosts, loopback or cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/). The first 500 characters of the response body are returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF, not blind.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16; response body returned via jsonify at app.py:17

trace.note: requests.get(target, timeout=5) - called with no validation; redirects followed by default
resp.text[:500] and the status code are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No guard on this path. ALLOWED_HOSTS (app.py:9) is only used in /partner. There is no scheme restriction, no hostname check, no IP/CIDR blocking, no allow_redirects=False, and no authentication decorator. Severity: HIGH, with redirect risk. Closed candidates: /partner (app.py:20-27) checks urlparse(target).hostname against the exact-match set ALLOWED_HOSTS before the request, which is the accepted closing pattern. It would only be exploitable if an allowlisted partner host served a malicious redirect, which counts as a trusted-service failure. /health (app.py:30-33) uses STATUS_URL from an environment variable, which is startup config and not per-request input.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the url query parameter, app.py:16 passes it unvalidated to requests.get (no auth decorator, scheme check, host check or allow_redirects=False), and app.py:17 returns the first 500 characters of the body, so this is full-read SSRF.
